agent_summary: Every upstream step of the haem scavenging chain is a gap in canine babesiosis: cfHb, haemopexin and haptoglobin have been measured only against controls or over time, and HO-1 and ADMA never; all have grade 2-3 human severity evidence and a canine assay, and cfHb (DS02, DS07 HBB), HMOX1 and HPX (DS06) are in public files. Not gaps: NO metabolites (Jacobson 2002, no severity signal) and the downstream lipid peroxidation readout (MDA, 3 severity-tested units). Surprise: both canine proteomic studies report haemopexin raised, not depleted, in infected dogs; haptoglobin findings are inconsistent (low, normal, raised).

mechanisms.human_direction: higher in severe malaria (falciparum and knowlesi), with AKI and in fatal cases; independently higher in sepsis non-survivors

cb_confirmed.what: plasma haemoglobin measured serially in experimental B. rossi Beagles (3 high-dose, 2 low-dose); rose by day 3 in the high-dose group; contrast is inoculum dose and time, not a severity/outcome grouping

mechanisms.testable_detail: DS02 cfhb (5 experimental B. rossi Beagles; dose groups and clinical scores, no outcome labels); DS07 master P60524 (HBB, 45% coverage); HBA P60529 is master_candidate only. Serum HBB peptides in DS07 may also reflect in vitro haemolysis.
mechanisms.notes: Jacobson 2002 (B. rossi, mild/severe/complicated groups) used free serum Hb as a covariate for nitric oxide metabolites; the abstract reports no cfHb-by-severity result, so it is not counted. CFH spectrophotometry is used in a canine sepsis model (purpose-bred Beagles), not formally validated. HU022 is brain tissue Hb by near-infrared spectroscopy, tangential.

mechanisms.human_direction: free haem (haemin, labile haem) higher and haemopexin lower in severe and fatal paediatric malaria; in sepsis haemopexin was not independently linked to death and in Angolan children haemopexin was not a risk factor

mechanisms.testable_detail: DS06 ENSCAFG00000006430_HPX (whole-blood RNA-seq of the DS02 Beagles: gene expression, not circulating protein; HPX is made in liver, so blood expression is a weak proxy). Not a master protein in DS07. Free haem itself is in no public file.
mechanisms.notes: Surprise: both canine proteomic studies report haemopexin HIGHER in infected dogs, opposite to the human 'depletion' direction. Canine haemopexin has only been quantified by mass spectrometry; no canine immunoassay validation found. Free/labile haem never measured in canine babesiosis.

mechanisms.human_direction: higher haptoglobin independently linked to lower in-hospital mortality in sepsis (effect confined to patients with detectable cfHb); in paediatric malaria haptoglobin was not a risk factor for severe disease

mechanisms.testable_detail: DS07 has haptoglobin only as master_candidate (P19006 HP and G1K2D9 LOC479668, 16% coverage): counts only with this note. No HP Ensembl ID in DS06 counts per reference_lookup, although CB082 names HP among haemolysis-cluster genes of the same Beagles. Not in DS02.
mechanisms.notes: Ulutas 2005 (pre-window) had 6 uncomplicated and 1 complicated dog, so no usable severity contrast. Canine Hp is a positive acute-phase protein, so consumption by cfHb and induction by inflammation pull in opposite directions; canine results are inconsistent (low, normal, raised). Haemolysis lowers measured Hp in the validated canine assay.

mechanisms.human_direction: plasma HO-1 higher in severe malaria (Gambian children) and higher HO-1 linked to death in cerebral malaria (Ugandan children); HMOX1 promoter repeat linked to severe disease/death; serum HO-1 higher in septic AKI

mechanisms.testable_detail: DS06 ENSCAFG00000001711_HMOX1 (whole-blood RNA-seq of the DS02 Beagles: gene expression, not circulating protein; human work shows neutrophils are the main blood HO-1 source, so blood expression is relevant). Not in DS07 or DS02.
mechanisms.notes: Zero PubMed hits for HO-1 in canine babesiosis. Plasma/splenic HO-1 measured in dogs by capture ELISA in visceral leishmaniasis (no formal canine validation).

mechanisms.testable_detail: No DS07 master, no DS06 genes in reference_lookup, nothing in DS02. NOx (Griess) or arginine would need archived serum.
mechanisms.notes: Severity units: Jacobson 2002 (B. rossi, mild/severe uncomplicated/complicated, not in the review, pre-window): serum NO metabolites did not separate severity or outcome; CH06 urinary arginine vs UPC (weak, renal axis only). NO metabolites are not the human exposure (endothelial NO bioavailability, plasma arginine:ADMA); those are unmeasured in dogs with babesiosis. ADMA split out as F1-11.

mechanisms.mechanism: ADMA and arginine bioavailability (plasma arginine:ADMA ratio)
mechanisms.human_direction: arginine:ADMA ratio lower in severe than non-severe malaria (adults) and low in severe paediatric malaria, inversely related to lactate and angiopoietin-2; ADMA itself higher in adults (linked to mortality in that group's work) but lower in children
cb_rejected: no CB article measured ADMA; CB053 measured SDMA (renal filtration marker), not ADMA

mechanisms.testable_detail: ADMA is a metabolite: not a DS07 protein, not a DS02 variable. DDAH/PRMT gene expression in DS06 not checked here (left to the assembly script). HPLC or ELISA on archived serum needed.
mechanisms.notes: SDMA (a renal filtration marker, not the NOS inhibitor) was severity-tested in B. rossi (higher in complicated: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ttbdis.2020.101406) and measured in B. canis (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ttbdis.2018.07.012); ADMA never. Canine ADMA by HPLC was linked to death in acute pancreatitis.

mechanisms.human_direction: plasma F2-isoprostanes higher in fatal falciparum malaria and with AKI needing dialysis; in sepsis isoprostanes lower when cfHb-associated oxidation is blocked (acetaminophen)

mechanisms.notes: Added as a check on the premise: the downstream oxidative-damage readout is already severity-tested in 3 canine units (mixed results), while the upstream haem scavenging chain (cfHb, free haem, haemopexin, haptoglobin, HO-1) is not. F2-isoprostanes never measured in canine babesiosis. CB499 has no DOI in articles.jsonl.
